topics.topic: Required outcome of concurrent first manual-budget creation
questions: When concurrent ensure_manual_budget calls race to create the first manual version, must both succeed and return the same version, or may one fail with PersistenceError?
When concurrent ensure_manual_budget calls race to create the first manual version, must the loser re-read and return the winner's version, or fail with PersistenceError?
When two concurrent calls both observe no manual version, must both succeed with the single resulting version, or may one fail with a persistence error?

quotes: `module:budget_management`. Return the project's one manual budget version, creating it empty when absent.

A18: at most one manual version per project; a new one is `inactive` and is
never activated implicitly; A13 (`budget.manual_version_create` only when it
is created).

Writes one `BudgetVersion` and one `AuditRecord` when none exists; otherwise
read-only.
judgement.divergence: A losing concurrent call either re-reads and returns the version created by the winner, so both callers succeed, or propagates the uniqueness failure as PersistenceError, so one caller receives HTTP 500; the losing staff caller notices.
judgement.why: The operation fixes uniqueness and ordinary create-or-return behavior but not the observable outcome when concurrent callers both observe absence.

witness.initial: An active project has no manual BudgetVersion, and two authorized staff progress-list requests are in flight.

outcomes: Both calls succeed with the single resulting manual version, and only one budget.manual_version_create audit exists.
One call succeeds, while the other propagates PersistenceError and its HTTP caller receives 500; one version and one audit exist.

topics.topic: Handling allocation amounts with more than two fractional digits
questions: How must correction allocation amounts with more than two fraction digits be handled: stored unchanged, rounded, or rejected?
How must correct_expense handle allocation amounts with more than two fraction digits: reject them, quantize them, or store them exactly despite the two-digit stored-money rule?

quotes:
Money is `Decimal` with 2 fraction digits, currency always `EUR`; rounding
  policy is a State 2 rule. Negative amounts never appear in stored records,
  with one named exception: an expense allocation amount (M26, M29);
  otherwise negative values exist only in derived values: balances, and
  the sums over such allocations (never clamped).

`Decimal`, 2 fraction digits, `ROUND_HALF_UP` at derivation boundaries;
  stored amounts are already 2-digit exact.

A9 (the total in EUR, non-negative), A19 (every section target of this
project, exact sum), A24, A13 (`expense.correct`); no intermediate state
commits. The allocation list must hold at least one instruction whatever
the total; an empty list is refused, a zero total included. An individual
amount is not otherwise checked (State 1 M26), so a zero total is corrected
with, for example, one zero allocation.

Updates the `Expense` and replaces its allocations; appends one
`AuditRecord`.
judgement.divergence: An implementer may store submitted three-decimal allocation amounts unchanged, quantize them to two digits before storage, or reject them to preserve the two-digit stored-money rule; the staff caller and later expense and financial views notice success versus rejection or changed allocation values.
judgement.why: The texts permit arbitrary-sign allocation amounts and say correct_expense performs no other individual check, while also requiring every stored monetary amount to be two-digit exact, without fixing quantization or rejection.

witness.initial: An active project contains an expense with total_amount EUR 10.00 that the acting staff member may correct.
events: The staff member calls correct_expense with total EUR 10.00 and allocations -0.001 and 10.001, whose exact sum is 10.00.
outcomes: The correction succeeds and the allocations are stored unchanged with three fractional digits.
The amounts are quantized or the correction is rejected to enforce two-digit stored amounts, changing the stored values or producing a 422 response.
witness.observer: The staff caller and readers of the corrected expense.
basis: `module:expense_management`. Correct an expense's facts and replace all its allocations.

The `PortalStore`, an `AuthorizedProjectContext`, the `expense_id`, the
supplier, the document date, the total, the inclusion flag and the complete
`AllocationInstruction` list.

An individual
amount is not otherwise checked (State 1 M26), so a zero total is corrected
with, for example, one zero allocation.

topics.topic: Propagation of runtime settings to use cases
questions: How do use cases receive deployment-specific settings such as staff_session_ttl_hours and viewer_session_ttl_days if create_runtime_app passes RuntimeSettings only to the store and transport guard and api.create_app accepts only PortalStore?
How do identity and other use-case operations receive the configured values when runtime passes settings only to PortalStore and transport_guard?

quotes:
The
settings handed here reach only the store and the transport guard: the
inner application and the use cases receive no `RuntimeSettings`; which
knobs a deployment can change is carried to States 6–7 (`SOURCE.md`).

A16 (normalized email), A17 (the session secret is issued for the new
`session_id`; only its hash is stored), R0-06 (fixed expiry of
`config.staff_session_ttl_hours`, twelve hours), A13: once the address has
normalized, exactly one audit on every outcome — `staff.login` success or
`staff.login_failed` rejected with no reason code.
judgement.why: The runtime operation denies RuntimeSettings to use cases while authenticate_staff requires a deployment-configurable staff-session TTL, so the required configured behavior has no allowed input path.

topics.topic: Allocation sequence for ServiceCredential key versions
questions: What key_version is assigned to a principal's first credential, and how is each later value derived?

quotes:
`ServiceCredentialIssue`: the new `ServiceCredential` with the next
`key_version` and the secret in plaintext, returned once. Of two
concurrent issuances for one principal that pick the same key version, the
uniqueness of (`service_principal_id`, `key_version`) lets one commit; the
other fails as a persistence failure and writes nothing.

A12, A17 (secret issued for the fresh `credential_id`; only the hash
stored); earlier credentials stay valid until revoked; A13
(`principal.credential_issue` with the key version).
judgement.divergence: The first credential may receive key_version 0 or 1, with later credentials incrementing from that base; the administrator sees the value in the issuance response and audit consumers see it in principal.credential_issue provenance.
judgement.why: The texts require a monotonic next key version but never fix the initial value from which the sequence begins.

topics.topic: Entity kind and ID for successful staff.login audits
questions: Which entity_kind and entity_id must the successful staff.login AuditRecord contain?

quotes:
A16 (normalized email), A17 (the session secret is issued for the new
`session_id`; only its hash is stored), R0-06 (fixed expiry of
`config.staff_session_ttl_hours`, twelve hours), A13: once the address has
normalized, exactly one audit on every outcome — `staff.login` success or
`staff.login_failed` rejected with no reason code. A rejection audit names the
account the normalized address matched as both actor and entity, also when
the account is not active, not verified or the password is wrong; actor and
entity are empty only when no account matched, and the actor kind is staff
in every case.

Writes one `StaffSession` and one `AuditRecord` per success; one
`AuditRecord` per rejection.
judgement.divergence: A successful staff.login audit may identify the affected entity as staff_account with the staff_id or as staff_session with the newly issued session_id; administrators and audit consumers observe different entity kinds and identifiers.
judgement.why: The operation requires a successful staff.login audit but specifies the actor/entity pairing only for rejected login audits, leaving the successful audit's affected entity open.
